p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** A routing table from *situation* to *target genre*, a companion table of misfiling smells that tell you a document landed in the wrong genre, and one worked example of the two-way linking law.

p.USE-IT-AT-THE-MOMENT-YOU-ARE-ABOUT-TO-WR: Use it at the moment you are about to write — before the genre is fixed by habit rather than choice.

p.READ-WRITE-AND-WIRE-THE-LINK: Read the situation, write to the target, and — where a link column is filled — wire the link before you close the file.

td.ROW-SITUATION-NEW-CONSTRAINT: A new constraint or invariant is discovered

td.fact: **Contract section**
Add a changelog line naming what changed and why

td.ROW-SITUATION-BIG-NARRATIVE-WHY: A big narrative "why we chose this"

td.fact: **Design doc**
Link it to the contract; add the back-link at the anchor

td.ROW-SITUATION-COMPETITOR-STUDY: A study of a competitor or ecosystem tool

td.fact: **Research doc**
Cite the version/date studied; it will be superseded
**Campaign plan**
Name the gate that ends each phase

td.ROW-SITUATION-WHERE-WORK-STANDS: Where the work stands right now

td.fact: **The checkpoint**
Overwrite the old state; do not append

td.ROW-SITUATION-DURABLE-CHOICE: A durable choice (library, constant, protocol shape)

td.fact: **Decision record at the contract anchor**
The long-form story, if any, goes in a linked design doc

td.ROW-SITUATION-STANDING-INSTRUCTION: A standing instruction every session needs

td.fact: **Boot file**
Keep it small; link out to the full protocol

p.two-rows-are-easy-to-confuse: Two rows are easy to confuse.

p.A-DURABLE-CHOICE-GOES-AT-THE-CONTRACT-AN: A **durable choice** goes *at the contract anchor* as a compact record — decision, why, alternatives, revisit trigger — because it is binding.

p.A-BIG-NARRATIVE-WHY-GOES-IN-A-DESIGN-DOC: A **big narrative why** goes in a *design doc* because it is lore.

p.MOST-DECISIONS-PRODUCE-BOTH: Most real decisions produce both: a tight record at the anchor, and — only when the reasoning is large — a linked design doc holding the full story.

p.THE-RECORD-IS-THE-CONTRACT-THE-DESIGN-DO: The record is the contract; the design doc is its footnote, not its replacement.

spanning.title: When a situation spans two genres

p.MANY-TASKS-LAND-ON-TWO-ROWS-AT-ONCE: Many real writing tasks land on two rows at once — a session that both settles a constraint *and* produced pages of reasoning is a contract edit *and* a design doc.

p.SPLIT-ALONG-THE-BINDING-LINE: That is not ambiguity to resolve by picking one; it is a signal to **split along the binding line**:

item.SPAN-THE-BINDING-HALF-GOES-TO-THE-CONTRA: The binding half — the constraint, the invariant, the chosen value — goes to the contract, in contract shape.

item.SPAN-THE-NARRATIVE-HALF-GOES-TO-THE-DESI: The narrative half — the forks, the precedents, the path — goes to the design doc, in story shape.

item.SPAN-THE-TWO-WAY-LINK-JOINS-THEM: The two-way link joins them, so neither half is lost and the authority is unambiguous.

p.THE-TELL-IS-THE-WORD-AND: The tell that you are facing a spanning situation is the word "and": "we decided the timeout is 600 s *and* here is the whole latency study."

p.THE-AND-IS-THE-SEAM-CUT-THERE: The "and" is the seam; cut there.

p.a-misfiled-document-gives-off-a-smell: A document in the wrong genre gives off a smell.

p.MOVE-THE-MISPLACED-MATERIAL-AND-LEAVE-A-: When you catch one, the fix is to move the misplaced material to its genre and leave a link behind — not to leave it where it is because moving is work.

td.ROW-SMELL-CONTRACT-QUOTES-HISTORY: A contract quotes three paragraphs of history

td.fact: Lore leaked into a contract
Move the history to a design doc; leave a one-line why + link

td.ROW-SMELL-DESIGN-DOC-CITED-AS-BINDING: A design doc is cited as if binding ("per the design doc we must…")

td.fact: A contract is hiding inside lore
Extract the normative sentence to the contract; the design doc keeps the story

td.ROW-SMELL-CHECKPOINT-OLDER-THAN-THE-RELE: A checkpoint entry is older than the last release

td.fact: State posing as truth
The checkpoint is stale; overwrite it — real invariants belong in a contract

td.ROW-SMELL-CAMPAIGN-PLAN-AS-SPEC: A campaign plan is quoted to justify a behaviour

td.fact: An execution doc treated as a spec
The behaviour's authority is the contract; the plan only tracked the work

td.ROW-SMELL-RESEARCH-PRESCRIBES: A research doc prescribes what *we* must build

td.fact: Research drifted into design/contract
Split: the external study stays research; our resulting choice becomes a contract decision

p.THE-UNIFYING-TELL: The unifying tell: **binding weight in a non-binding genre, or narrative bulk in a binding one.**

p.genre-and-authority-have-come-apart: Either way the genre and the authority have come apart, which is exactly the confusion genre typing exists to prevent.

linking-example.title: The linking law, worked

p.easy-to-state-and-easy-to-half-do: The two-way link is easy to state and easy to half-do.

p.here-is-the-full-shape: Here is the full shape, both ends wired.

p.AT-THE-CONTRACT-A-RELATED-LINE-POINTS-OU: At the contract — a `Related` line points *out* to the lore, so a session reading the contract during boot finds the rationale without being told it exists:

p.AT-THE-DESIGN-DOC-THE-HEADER-NAMES-THE-C: At the design doc — the header names the contract section it explains, so a reader who arrives at the lore first can walk back to the authoritative value:

p.BOTH-ENDS-WIRED-MEANS-EITHER-SIDE-REACHE: Now a cold reader entering from *either* side reaches the other, and the precedence line in the design-doc header records — in-place — who wins if they ever drift.

p.what-the-pair-of-links-buys: That single pair of links is the difference between lore that survives a cold start and lore that is silently lost at the next session boundary.

item.SUM-A-DECISION-PRODUCES-BOTH: A decision usually produces both a compact record at the contract anchor and — if large — a linked design doc; the record is binding, the design doc is its footnote.

item.SUM-SMELLS-FLAG-MISFILINGS: Smells flag misfilings: history in a contract, a design doc cited as binding, a checkpoint older than the last release.

item.SUM-WIRE-BOTH-DIRECTIONS-OR-NEITHER: Wire both link directions or neither — a one-way link loses the lore from the other side.
